4. The defendant contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint and contending, inter alia, that the suit was not maintainable in its present form and was barred by limitation. The suit was also not maintainable for want of cause of action. The positive case of the defendant was that the plaintiff proposed to sell 'Ka' scheduled land to him to which he agreed. The consideration for the land was fixed at Taka 70,000 (taka seventy thousand) only and the parties being closely related to each other, no bainapatra was executed. The defendant paid Taka 60,000 (taka sixty thousand) to the plaintiff in two installments and in lieu of the remaining amount of Taka 10,000 (taka ten thousand) only, the plaintiff demanded 'Ga' scheduled land to which he .agreed and at the advice of the scribe instead of sale deed, a deed of exchange was executed and registered on 19-8-1990. The suit was filed on false pleas with a view to harassing the defendant. After the filing of the suit, there was a village salish wherein it was decided that the defendant would transfer 0.13½ acre of land to the plaintiff by a registered deed in order to avoid future problem and as per terms of the salishnama dated 26-10-1991, the plaintiff was supposed to file solenama in the suit, but he killed time on this or that plea and ultimately refused to file the solenama and hence, the suit was liable to be dismissed with costs. 

 9. The trial Court decreed the suit on the clear finding that exhibit-'Ka', the impugned deed, was created by the defendant in collusion with the deed writer showing the exchange of 'Ka' scheduled land of the plaintiff with the 'Ga' scheduled land of the defendant. In coming to the said finding, the trial Court observed that it was simply impossible to exchange 1.41¼ acres of land, i.e. the 'Ka' scheduled land with 0.16½ acre of land, i.e. the 'Ga' scheduled land. The trial Court came to the further finding that there was no talk of sale of the 'Ka' scheduled land at Taka 70,000 as claimed by the defendant and that the defendant did not pay any money to the plaintiff at all. The trial Court found the suit maintainable in its present form. The Appellate Court did not reverse the above findings of fact of the trial Court and in a cumbersome way came to the finding that the terms of the salishnama proved that the plaintiff executed and registered the impugned deed, exhibit-'Ka' within his full knowledge “(স্বজ্ঞানে) Sound mind (সুস্থ মস্তিকে) The Appellate Court relying on the salishnama came to the further finding that since the plaintiff agreed to exchange 'Kha' scheduled land (out of his 'Ka' scheduled land) with the 'Ga' scheduled land of the defendant, but the defendant in collusion with the deed writer created the impugned deed (exhibit 'Ka') showing exchange of the 'Ka' scheduled land with the 'Ca' scheduled land and that he ought to have filed a suit for rectification of the deed under section 31 of the Act and that his present suit under section 39 of the Act was not maintainable. In coming to the said finding, the Appellate Court relied upon one of the terms of the salishnama (exhibit-'Uma') that the defendant would transfer 0.13½ acre of land from 3(three) plots to the plaintiff.
